h33-h33-2-b2-TRACKBt1p0-20261023-7bc435f.hypothesis: R0 dots that cannot be chained into a >=1.0 km strike-consistent trace are mostly ridge-detector speckles and catalogue-truncated fragments; spending their mass on densifying/continuing >=1.0 km traces raises live DTI, because line-like new-fault truth pays a dot whose kernel credit exceeds ~0.2*DTI and continuous along-strike coverage collects that credit on many truth pixels.
h33-h33-2-b2-TRACKBt1p0-20261023-7bc435f.mechanism: Basin-and-Range normal faults are km-scale planar strands; GeoDAWN 400 m line spacing (kernel radius 300 m) blurs but does not create km-long collinear ridge chains by chance. Chaining R0 dots at <=4.5 px follows the H19-5 ridge strike, so a >=1.0 km span component is a strand, while sub-km fragments are where a 121k-px ridge support thinned at 2.8 px leaves isolated BFS artefacts. Refill within 6 px of surviving traces fills 300 m kernel gaps and short tip extensions along those strands.
h33-h33-2-b2-TRACKBt1p0-20261023-7bc435f.non_fault_mimic: Collinear Lake Lahontan shoreline benches, alluvial-fan distributary channels and basalt flow margins can chain into km-long lineaments with no brittle slip; they would absorb the refilled mass exactly like a fault strand.

h33-h33-2-b2-TRACKBt1p2-20261023-3322bd7.hypothesis: Raising the trace threshold to >=1.2 km removes additional short strands that are genuine fault tips and step-over relays; the gain over R0 is therefore smaller than at 1.0 km, bracketing where fragment removal turns from cleaning to amputation.
h33-h33-2-b2-TRACKBt1p2-20261023-3322bd7.mechanism: Fault displacement-length scaling puts many secondary strands at 1.0-1.2 km; Faulds-style step-overs and terminations -- where geothermal systems sit on known faults and where new geometry is most likely -- live precisely in this length band, so a stricter threshold starts deleting the discovery targets.
h33-h33-2-b2-TRACKBt1p2-20261023-3322bd7.non_fault_mimic: Terrace risers and fan-head trenches also concentrate at 1-1.2 km lengths, so any residual gain could still be shoreline/fan lineaments rather than faults.

h33-h33-2-b2-TRACKBt1p5-20261023-ab92778.hypothesis: At >=1.5 km the filter deletes whole secondary fault systems (sub-parallel splays, relay ramps and intersection branches under 1.5 km span); the variant loses live DTI despite cleaner traces, closing the dose-response from above.
h33-h33-2-b2-TRACKBt1p5-20261023-ab92778.mechanism: Damage-zone secondary strands are commonly 0.5-1.5 km long and sit 100-400 m from master faults; they are exactly the 'newly mapped geometry of existing systems' the organizer counts as new fault (Forum #11536), so removing them spends the budget only on master-strand densification with saturating kernel credit.
